title: The unitary integral with two independent diagonal sources
notes: Kazakov asks to calculate \(\int d\Omega\,\exp\sum_{\mu=1}^{2}\operatorname{Tr}(\Omega^\dagger p_\mu\Omega q_\mu)\), with diagonal \(p_\mu,q_\mu\), and says that the two-dimensional case has not been calculated.
statement: For prescribed diagonal complex \(N\times N\) matrices \(P_1,P_2,Q_1,Q_2\), determine \(Z_N=\int_{U(N)}\exp\{\sum_{\mu=1}^{2}\operatorname{Tr}(U^*P_\mu UQ_\mu)\}\,dU\), where Haar measure has mass one. Distinguish an exact convergent series, an efficient finite formula, and a useful large-\(N\) analysis.
reconstruction: Haar normalization, complex parameters and the distinction among meanings of evaluation are editorial specifications. The notebook states no particular target form of answer.
fate: \citet[Eq.~(3), Sections~2.2--2.3 and Appendix]{holguin2024multimatrix} study this same integral, obtaining an explicit \(U(2)\) expression and a \(U(3)\) expansion; their preprint appeared on 6 July 2023 and the article on 4 April 2024. They also identify the obstruction to a naive extension of the one-source localization formula. The chapter supplies an explicitly labelled rederivation and general convergent Haar expansion, not a claim of a new closed solution. Their angular convention in equation~(2.16) has total mass one quarter; comparison with this chapter\textquoteright s probability Haar measure therefore includes an overall normalization, not a correction of the paper.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, exact series evaluation is available and the two-dimensional unitary rank is explicit. A compact formula comparable to the one-source determinant, together with the desired general large-\(N\) control, is not supplied by the cited work; these stronger targets must not be conflated with the existence of an exact evaluation series.
worth: Worth developing in a bounded form: a checked finite-rank formula and a convergent expansion with an error bound make the original computational question concrete without claiming a general closed-form solution.

title: Expansion near the identity and planar perturbation theory
notes: The notes put \(\Omega=e^{iA}\), isolate a Gaussian part, expand the rest of the exponential and the Haar measure, and retain planar diagrams.
statement: An expansion about a specified nondegenerate saddle of a unitary matrix integral produces Gaussian Wick contractions and interaction vertices, including the Jacobian of exponential coordinates. At fixed formal order, double-line contractions are sorted by the Euler characteristic of their ribbon graph; planar terms are the leading powers of \(N\) under the usual matrix scaling.
reconstruction: The saddle and normalization conditions are necessary additions. The notebook does not justify a globally valid identity-centred expansion.
fate: This is the established matrix-model diagrammatic method of \citet[Sections~2--3]{bessisitzyksonzuber1980graphical}. It does not itself establish convergence or select the dominant saddle of the multi-source integral.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: One-site reduction of lattice gauge theory
notes: A product of \(d\) unitary integrals with plaquette traces is asserted to be equivalent to the ordinary gauge theory as \(N\to\infty\).
statement: The Eguchi--Kawai loop-equation reduction requires, in addition to large-\(N\) factorization, the unbroken centre symmetry that annihilates open reduced loops. The unrestricted equivalence of the original one-site model at every coupling is false; in the relevant weak-coupling regime the centre symmetry can break.
fate: \citet{eguchikawai1982reduction} proposed the reduction in 1982. \citet[abstract and model construction]{bhanothellerneuberger1982quenched} identified the symmetry-breaking obstruction and proposed quenching in the same year. This also connects with occurrences 1982-565.3--1982-565.6, but is not identical to the earlier specific free-energy problem.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Two-matrix Ising model on random quadrangulations
notes: The integral has Gaussian coupling \(2cuv\) and separate quartic vertices \(u^4+v^4\); it is said to count two-coloured quadrangular decompositions with a weight for interfaces.
statement: Treated as a formal expansion of a normalized two-Hermitian-matrix Gaussian integral with positive-definite quadratic covariance, the connected free energy sums connected orientable ribbon graphs. Quartic vertices are assigned one of two colours; dualization gives quadrangulations with an Ising spin on each dual face or original vertex, according to convention. Graphs carry automorphism factors, and the mixed propagator fixes the domain-wall weight.
reconstruction: Formal expansion, connectedness, automorphism weights and the distinction between the Gaussian parameter \(c\) and an exponential Ising coupling have been supplied. The displayed \(e^{2cm}\) cannot simply use the same \(c\) as the quadratic matrix coupling.
fate: \citet{kazakov1986ising} gives the exact planar Ising solution on a fluctuating lattice. The journal article appeared on 8 December 1986, shortly after the recorded 24 November talk; publication metadata verifies the identification, while the precise notebook parametrization needs the original conventions. The general graphical framework is already in \citet{bessisitzyksonzuber1980graphical}.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Hermitian diagonalization and the Vandermonde square
notes: Diagonalization of each matrix produces \(\Delta(x)^2\Delta(y)^2\) and one relative unitary integration.
statement: For an integrable conjugation-invariant function on Hermitian \(N\times N\) matrices, Lebesgue measure disintegrates into a convention-dependent constant times \(\prod_i dx_i\,\Delta(x)^2\) and normalized orbit measure. For two matrices the relative eigenbasis is Haar distributed; stabilizers and eigenvalue permutations are included in the constant.
fate: \citet[Hermitian eigenvalue reduction]{bessisitzyksonzuber1980graphical} use precisely this reduction in matrix enumeration. The square, rather than a single Vandermonde, is essential before the angular integral.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: The one-source unitary orbital integral
notes: The angular integral is written as \(\det(e^{2cx_i y_j})/[\Delta(x)\Delta(y)]\), without a normalizing factor.
statement: For normalized Haar measure and pairwise distinct eigenvalues, \[\int_{U(N)} e^{t\operatorname{Tr}(XUYU^*)}\,dU=\left(\prod_{j=1}^{N-1}j!\right)t^{-N(N-1)/2}\frac{\det(e^{tx_i y_j})}{\Delta(x)\Delta(y)}.\] Coincident eigenvalues and \(t=0\) are interpreted by analytic continuation of the removable singularities.
fate: The matrix-integral form is the established formula in \citet{itzyksonzuber1980planar}. The omitted \(t\)-dependent factor matters if the notebook equality is literal; some eigenvalue-independent constants can instead be absorbed into a partition-function normalization.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Biorthogonal polynomials and the partition-function product
notes: Polynomials are orthogonal for a two-variable weight. The notebook gives a moment determinant and a product of norms as the matrix integral.
statement: For a bilinear moment functional \(\langle f,g\rangle=\iint f(x)g(y)w(x,y)\,dx\,dy\), assume all leading moment minors are nonzero. Unique monic families \(P_n,Q_n\) satisfy \(\langle P_n,Q_m\rangle=h_n\delta_{nm}\). A determinant formula for a monic polynomial must be divided by its leading moment minor. For symmetric weight one may take \(P_n=Q_n\). Andr\'eief expansion gives the labelled eigenvalue integral \(N!\prod_{n=0}^{N-1}h_n\), before any angular normalization.
fate: The orthogonal and biorthogonal reduction belongs to the established matrix method; see \citet{bessisitzyksonzuber1980graphical} and the two-matrix application in \citet{kazakov1986ising}. The factorial and index shifts depend on whether the eigenvalues are ordered; the notebook does not state that convention.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Parametric planar free energy and its critical points
notes: The notes give \(g(z)=z/(1-3z)^2-c^2z+3c^2z^3\), an integral expression for \(F\), and locate singularities by \(g^{\prime}(z)=0\).
statement: On the branch of the stated parametric solution analytic at the Gaussian point, critical points of the inverse relation \(z=z(g)\) occur where \(g^{\prime}(z)=0\), unless a singularity or cancellation changes the local analysis. Extracting asymptotics of map coefficients additionally requires identifying the dominant singularity and the order of vanishing. The displayed free-energy integral depends on the partition-function normalization.
fate: The explicit two-matrix Ising solution is identified by \citet{kazakov1986ising}. Its publication metadata is verified, but a line-by-line match of the notebook free-energy normalization is not asserted. The inverse-function criterion explains the stated mechanism; the notebook alone does not justify the claimed global asymptotics.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the planar Ising matrix model is exactly solved. The present identification is of the model and critical-point mechanism; the precise additive and multiplicative normalization of the notebook expression remains an editorial qualification.

title: Faltings and p-adic string theory
notes: Gelfand mentions Faltings in connection with p-adic strings, without a mathematical assertion or bibliographic identification.
statement: The record preserves a thematic pointer to p-adic approaches to string theory. It specifies neither a p-adic curve, a moduli problem, nor an amplitude to calculate.
fate: No exact theorem or problem can be recovered from this sentence. It is not legitimate to identify it with an arbitrary later paper on p-adic strings.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the mathematical referent of this particular remark remains unidentified; this is a source limitation, not a claim that the subject was undeveloped.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Genus enumeration of oriented polygon gluings
notes: Pair the sides of an oriented \(2n\)-gon with opposite orientation; cyclic rotations remain distinguishable. Count the resulting surfaces by genus.
statement: Let \(\epsilon_g(n)\) count perfect matchings of the labelled sides of a fixed oriented \(2n\)-gon, glued orientation-reversingly, whose quotient is a connected closed oriented surface of genus \(g\). The number is zero for \(2g>n\). Labels fix a boundary root, so no quotient by rotation is taken.
fate: \citet[Theorem~2 and its recurrence]{harerzagier1986euler} had already solved this enumeration in 1986. The later Kazakov lecture 1986-702 gives the matrix-integral derivation. The connection is to orbifold Euler characteristics of moduli spaces; Teichm\"uller space itself is contractible.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Level-one holomorphic modular and cusp forms
notes: The notes impose the weight transformation law, Fourier expansion and vanishing at infinity, but write determinant \(\pm1\) and a negative Fourier exponent.
statement: For even \(k\), a level-one modular form is holomorphic on \(\mathbb H\), satisfies \(f((az+b)/(cz+d))=(cz+d)^kf(z)\) for \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{smallmatrix}\right)\in SL_2(\mathbb Z)\), and is holomorphic at the cusp. Thus \(f(z)=\sum_{n\ge0}a_nq^n\), \(q=e^{2\pi iz}\); a cusp form has \(a_0=0\). Matrices of determinant \(-1\) do not act holomorphically on \(\mathbb H\) by this formula.
fate: This is the classical setting fixed explicitly in \citet[Section~1]{zagier1977quadratic} and \citet[Section~1]{kohnenzagier1984periods}. The manuscript signs are faithfully transcribed but mathematically inconsistent with its later definition of \(q\).
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Integral bases, small weights, and the discriminant form
notes: The notes list the vanishing of several cusp-form spaces, integral Fourier coefficients, the Eisenstein series and \(\Delta=q-24q^2+252q^3-\cdots\).
statement: For level one, \(M_*\) over \(\mathbb C\) is generated by \(E_4,E_6\), and \(S_k=\Delta M_{k-12}\), where \(\Delta=(E_4^3-E_6^2)/1728\). In particular \(S_k=0\) for \(k=2,4,6,8,10,14\) and all odd \(k\). A basis with integral Fourier coefficients can be chosen; this does not mean every complex linear combination has integral coefficients.
fate: \citet[Section~1 and examples]{kohnenzagier1984periods} use the rational Fourier structure and the discriminant form. The displayed coefficients and vanishing statements are standard pre-1987 material.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Normalized Eisenstein series and Fourier coefficients
notes: The primitive lattice sum defining \(E_k\) has denominator power 2, whereas the transformation weight and subsequent examples use \(k\).
statement: For even \(k\ge4\), \(E_k(z)=\tfrac12\sum_{(c,d)=1}(cz+d)^{-k}=1-(2k/B_k)\sum_{n\ge1}\sigma_{k-1}(n)q^n\). Absolute convergence justifies rearrangement. In particular \(E_4=1+240(q+9q^2+28q^3+73q^4+\cdots)\). Weight 2 requires quasimodular or nonholomorphic corrections.
fate: The Eisenstein normalizations and their products are treated in \citet[Sections~1--2]{kohnenzagier1984periods}. The denominator exponent in the notebook is an error, not a different normalization.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Hecke eigenforms and coefficient multiplicativity
notes: An Euler form is characterized by multiplicative coefficients, and the Hecke operators have a simultaneous eigenbasis.
statement: On \(S_k(SL_2(\mathbb Z))\), the usual Hecke operators commute and are self-adjoint for the Petersson product. A normalized eigenform \(f=\sum a_nq^n\), \(a_1=1\), satisfies \(T_nf=a_nf\) and \(a_ma_n=\sum_{d\mid(m,n)}d^{k-1}a_{mn/d^2}\). Coprime multiplicativity alone omits the prime-power relation needed for the full Hecke characterization.
fate: \citet[Section~1]{zagier1977quadratic} fixes the normalized eigenbasis and its eigenvalues; \citet[Section~1]{kohnenzagier1984periods} uses the same Hecke structure in the period rationality theorem.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Normalization of the slash action and Hecke operators
notes: The \(GL_2^+\) slash action includes \(\det(A)^{k/2}\). The displayed coset definition of \(T_n\) also has a factor \(1/2\), while the examples have \(T_1=1\).
statement: Use \((f|_kA)(z)=\det(A)^{k/2}(cz+d)^{-k}f(Az)\) and \(T_nf=n^{k/2-1}\sum_{A\in SL_2(\mathbb Z)\backslash M_n}f|_kA\), with each coset counted once. Then \(T_1=1\) and \(T_2f=2^{k-1}f(2z)+\tfrac12f(z/2)+\tfrac12f((z+1)/2)\). A separate factor \(1/2\) is appropriate only if both signs are deliberately counted.
fate: The normalization is the one underlying \citet[Section~1]{zagier1977quadratic}. The notebook combines the quotient convention with the double-counting factor; its concrete \(T_2\) example identifies the intended correction.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Weighted Bergman reproducing identity
notes: A half-plane integral reproduces a holomorphic function with constant \((-1)^{k/2}\pi/[2^{k-2}(k-1)]\).
statement: For even \(k\ge2\), \(w\in\mathbb H\), and a holomorphic function in the weighted Bergman space for measure \(y^{k-2}dx\,dy\), \[\int_{\mathbb H}\frac{f(z)y^{k-2}}{(\bar z-w)^k}\,dx\,dy=\frac{(-1)^{k/2}\pi}{2^{k-2}(k-1)}f(w).\] A growth or integrability hypothesis is essential; an arbitrary holomorphic function need not have the displayed integral.
fate: This kernel calculation is the analytic ingredient in \citet[Section~2]{zagier1977quadratic}. Its use for automorphic forms follows by unfolding a convergent Poincar\'e kernel, not by assuming every modular form is square-integrable over the entire half-plane.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: The Hecke kernel and its spectral trace
notes: A determinant-\(n\) matrix sum is expanded in a Hecke eigenbasis; setting the two variables on the appropriate diagonal yields \(\operatorname{Tr}T_n\).
statement: For even \(k>2\), the convergent holomorphic kernel obtained by summing the weighted Bergman kernel over integer matrices of determinant \(n\) represents the normalized Hecke operator on the finite-dimensional Petersson space \(S_k\). Its spectral expansion runs over \(\dim S_k\) eigenforms, with reciprocal Petersson norms and eigenvalues \(a_j(n)\). Integrating the diagonal gives \(\sum_{j=1}^{\dim S_k}a_j(n)\).
fate: \citet[Section~2 and equations~(14)--(19)]{zagier1977quadratic} develops this kernel method. The notebook upper summation bound \(n\) in the eigenform sum is a transcription-faithful mathematical slip: the number of eigenforms does not depend on the Hecke index.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Binary quadratic forms in the trace calculation
notes: Matrices of determinant \(n\) are reindexed by \(t=a+d\) and \(Q=[c,d-a,-b]\), with discriminant \(t^2-4n\), and the associated real-analytic kernel is integrated.
statement: The matrix-to-form substitution has \(\operatorname{disc}(Q)=t^2-4n\). The elliptic contribution comes from negative discriminants with stabilizer weights. Positive nonsquare discriminants cancel in the specialized trace calculation, whereas positive squares contribute the divisor term; the scalar discriminant-zero contribution must also be retained. Sign pairs must be counted consistently with the initial factor \(1/2\).
fate: \citet[Section~1, equations~(17)--(23), and Sections~3--4]{zagier1977quadratic} explicitly separates these cases. The notebook sentence about discriminants cannot be read as saying that all nonnegative contributions vanish.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: The Eichler--Selberg trace formula at level one
notes: The final trace is a finite sum of weighted class numbers and a divisor correction.
statement: For even \(k\ge4\) and \(n\ge1\), put \(p_k(t,n)=[X^{k-2}](1-tX+nX^2)^{-1}\). Write \(H(D)\) for the Hurwitz weighted class number of negative discriminant \(D\), with \(H(0)=-1/12\). Then \[\operatorname{Tr}(T_n|S_k)=-\frac12\sum_{t^2\le4n}p_k(t,n)H(t^2-4n)-\frac12\sum_{d\mid n}\min(d,n/d)^{k-1}.\] The \(D=0\) convention incorporates the scalar term when \(n\) is a square.
fate: This is the pre-existing Eichler--Selberg formula, recovered in \citet[Section~1, equation~(23)]{zagier1977quadratic}. The notebook gives its kernel derivation, not a new trace formula. Weight 2 is excluded because its correction terms differ.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Hurwitz weights and the trace polynomials
notes: A table lists class numbers and \(p_2=1,p_3=t,p_4=t^2-n\), with a tentative identification as Legendre polynomials.
statement: The polynomial recursion is \(p_{k+1}=tp_k-np_{k-1}\), so \(p_k(t,n)=n^{(k-2)/2}U_{k-2}(t/(2\sqrt n))\) for \(n>0\), where \(U_j\) is the Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind. Hurwitz numbers include imprimitive forms: \(H(-3)=1/3\), \(H(-4)=1/2\), \(H(-16)=3/2\), and \(H(-32)=3\).
fate: \citet[equations~(18), (20)]{zagier1977quadratic} specifies both the generating polynomial and the imprimitive class-number weights. The notebook table entry 2 for discriminant \(-32\) counts only the primitive order and is not the required Hurwitz number.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Nonholomorphic Eisenstein series and Rankin unfolding
notes: The primitive Eisenstein sum is integrated against an invariant function, leaving the Mellin transform of its constant Fourier term.
statement: For \(\operatorname{Re}s>1\), set \(E(z,s)=\tfrac12\sum_{(c,d)=1}y^s|cz+d|^{-2s}\). For a smooth automorphic \(F\) with sufficient decay, \[\int_{SL_2(\mathbb Z)\backslash\mathbb H}F(z)E(z,s)\,\frac{dx\,dy}{y^2}=\int_0^\infty a_0(y)y^{s-2}\,dy,\quad a_0(y)=\int_0^1F(x+iy)\,dx.\] Complex conjugation may be inserted consistently on both sides, not on one side only.
fate: \citet[Section~1]{zagier1981eisenstein} gives this transform, and \citet[Sections~1--2]{zagier1982rankin} treats functions of nonrapid decay by explicit regularization. The latter paper was received in June 1981 and published in volume 28 (1982).
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Completion, continuation, and poles of the Eisenstein series
notes: The notes assert a functional equation using \((2\pi)^s\Gamma(s)E(z,s)\), and list poles at 1 and half of zeta zeros.
statement: The correct completion for the primitive sum is \(E^*(z,s)=\pi^{-s}\Gamma(s)\zeta(2s)E(z,s)\). It is invariant under \(s\mapsto1-s\), with its standard simple poles at 0 and 1. The uncompleted series has residue \(3/\pi\) at 1; zeros of \(\zeta(2s)\) give possible poles after division, subject to cancellation. Multiplying by \(\Gamma(s)\) alone does not give the stated symmetry.
fate: \citet[Section~1]{zagier1981eisenstein} supplies the exact completion and residue. The missing zeta factor and the power of \(\pi\) are material errors in the recorded formula.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Horocycle averages and the Riemann hypothesis
notes: The constant term is said to tend to the average over the fundamental domain, with oscillations of size \(y^{3/4}\). The normalization \(3/\pi\) disappears in one displayed formula.
statement: For suitable smooth compactly supported automorphic \(F\), \(a_0(y)\to(3/\pi)\int_{\Gamma\backslash\mathbb H}F\,d\mu\) as \(y\downarrow0\). Mellin poles associated with zeta zeros control finer terms. A bound of the form \(O_F(y^{3/4-\varepsilon})\) for all such tests is a Riemann-hypothesis strength assertion; it is not an unconditional rate for every measurable invariant function.
fate: \citet[Section~1 and the horocycle discussion]{zagier1981eisenstein} explains the connection between equidistribution remainders and zeta zeros. The current unresolved status of RH is independently recorded by \citet{clay2026riemann}.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, qualitative equidistribution under the stated test-function hypotheses is established; the universal RH-strength remainder is conditional. The notebook should not be read as an announced proof of RH.
worth: The statement is useful as an exact conditional implication and a normalization check, but proving its full Riemann-hypothesis strength is not a bounded chapter project.

title: Quadratic-field periods and toroidal automorphic forms
notes: Toroidal integrals of the Eisenstein series contain a quadratic-field zeta function, and therefore vanish at suitable zeros of \(\zeta(s)\).
statement: For a nonsplit rational torus attached to a quadratic field, the appropriately normalized toroidal period of an Eisenstein series factors into a Hecke L-function product. The toroidal subspace consists of automorphic forms whose periods over every such torus vanish. Analytic continuation and the exact normalization are required at zeros and poles; one cannot simply substitute a singular quotient.
fate: \citet[Sections~2--4]{zagier1981eisenstein} develops the proposal already before the talk. \citet[main theorem]{cornelissenlorscheid2011toroidal}, first circulated in June 2009 and revised in August 2011, identifies the Eisenstein-derivative part through zero multiplicities and the cuspidal part through central L-values.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the later structural theorem clarifies the toroidal space, including derivatives at multiple zeros. It does not prove that all zeta zeros lie on the critical line.

title: The toroidal spectral strategy for the Riemann hypothesis
notes: The notes form a span \(W\) of quadratic-form transforms and an orthogonal complement \(V\), note Laplacian invariance, and suggest that unitarity of the corresponding representation would imply RH.
statement: The recognizable strategy seeks a spectral realization of the toroidal automorphic space that forces the relevant Eisenstein parameters onto the critical line. The necessary conclusion is temperedness of the relevant constituents; unitarity alone allows complementary-series representations and is insufficient. One must specify the topology, invariant pairing, spectral identification and exclusion of non-tempered constituents. Formal invariance under the Laplacian proves none of these requirements.
fate: \citet[final sections]{zagier1981eisenstein} gives the earlier strategy and its difficulties. \citet[Introduction and main results]{cornelissenlorscheid2011toroidal} identifies the toroidal spectrum and explicitly states the RH connection in terms of temperedness. It does not prove that needed restriction. \citet{clay2026riemann} confirms that RH remains open.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the algebraic toroidal spectrum is substantially understood, but the required critical-line spectral restriction is unproved. The notebook\textquoteright s unqualified appeal to unitarity does not establish RH.
worth: Worth preserving as a precisely conditional spectral strategy; the notebook leaves the functional-analytic object too unspecified for a new proof attempt here.

title: Two-colour map enumeration with a prescribed interface length
notes: At the opening, maps with fixed numbers of black and white triangles and a prescribed boundary between colours are proposed.
statement: Count rooted orientable planar maps of the specified face degrees with two face colours, tracking separately the numbers of both colours and the number of edges separating colours. Equivalently, use the corresponding formal two-matrix generating function, with separate vertex variables and mixed-propagator weight; unrooted counts require automorphism weights.
fate: The two-matrix Ising solution of \citet{kazakov1986ising} treats this enumeration framework. The notebook does not fix rooting, degenerate faces, or a requested coefficient formula, so identification with the exact quartic parameterization is partial. The same variant returns at the end of record 702.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Even and negative zeta-values and moduli Euler characteristics
notes: Bernoulli formulas for \(\zeta(2n)\) and \(\zeta(1-2g)\) are related to the Euler characteristic of the moduli space; the list gives \(\zeta(-3)=1/252\).
statement: For \(n\ge1\), \(\zeta(2n)=(-1)^{n+1}B_{2n}(2\pi)^{2n}/[2(2n)!]\) and \(\zeta(1-2n)=-B_{2n}/(2n)\). For \(g\ge2\), \(\chi_{\mathrm{orb}}(\mathcal M_{g,1})=\zeta(1-2g)\) and \(\chi_{\mathrm{orb}}(\mathcal M_g)=\zeta(1-2g)/(2-2g)\). Thus \(\zeta(-3)=1/120\), while \(\zeta(-5)=-1/252\).
fate: The moduli-space formula is the main theorem of \citet{harerzagier1986euler}, published before this lecture. Marking one point and using the orbifold Euler characteristic are indispensable; replacing these by the ordinary Euler characteristic of unpointed Teichm\"uller space is false.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Eisenstein products and recurrences for even zeta-values
notes: Identities such as \(E_4^2=E_8\) and \(E_4E_6=E_{10}\) yield recurrences for even zeta-values.
statement: Level-one dimensions give \(E_4^2=E_8\) and \(E_4E_6=E_{10}\) for normalized Eisenstein series. Comparing their Fourier coefficients and the Bernoulli normalization produces convolution identities for divisor sums and even zeta-values. At weights with cusp forms, the Eisenstein product generally has a nonzero cuspidal component, which must be retained.
fate: \citet[initial sections]{kohnenzagier1984periods} supplies the Eisenstein-product framework used later in the lecture. The assertion is an established technique, with the small-weight identities representing special dimension-one cases.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Mellin transform and functional equation of a cusp-form L-function
notes: The completed Dirichlet series is expressed as an integral of \(f(iy)\), and inversion gives the reflection formula.
statement: If \(f(z)=\sum_{n\ge1}a_nq^n\in S_k(SL_2(\mathbb Z))\), then initially in a right half-plane \(\Lambda(f,s)=(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)\sum a_nn^{-s}=\int_0^\infty f(iy)y^{s-1}\,dy\). Cuspidal decay at both ends makes the integral entire, and \(\Lambda(f,s)=(-1)^{k/2}\Lambda(f,k-s)\). This applies to each cusp form, without an eigenform hypothesis; Euler products need that additional hypothesis.
fate: \citet[Section~1]{kohnenzagier1984periods} uses precisely these completed values and their functional equation in defining period polynomials.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: The two periods of a normalized Hecke eigenform
notes: The critical values split into even and odd groups, each rationally proportional to a period; the two periods are said probably to be transcendental.
statement: For a normalized level-one Hecke eigenform \(f\) with coefficient field \(K_f\), there are nonzero periods \(\Omega_f^\pm\), defined up to \(K_f^\times\), such that the appropriately parity-normalized critical values \(L(f,m)/( (2\pi i)^m\Omega_f^{(-1)^m})\), \(1\le m\le k-1\), lie in \(K_f\). For rational Fourier coefficients, the normalized period ratios are rational. Absolute transcendence is a separate assertion and depends on specifying the normalization.
fate: The period theorem predates the lecture; \citet[Theorem~1 and period-polynomial discussion]{kohnenzagier1984periods} gives the rational structures used here. The notebook\textquoteright s transcendence aside is not a proved part of that theorem.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Critical periods of the discriminant form
notes: A table expresses the integrals \(r_n=\int_0^\infty\Delta(iy)y^n\,dy\) in two periods, including a denominator 691.
statement: For the real-coefficient weight-12 discriminant form, \(r_n=(2\pi)^{-n-1}\Gamma(n+1)L(\Delta,n+1)\), \(0\le n\le10\), and \(r_n=r_{10-n}\). The even-indexed and odd-indexed period vectors each span a rational line. Numerical values of the generators have no invariant meaning until the rational scaling convention is fixed.
fate: \citet[examples and tables for weight 12]{kohnenzagier1984periods} gives the exact rational period relations. The occurrence of 691 belongs to these exact arithmetic ratios, not to a floating-point inference.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Rankin unfolding of products of Eisenstein series
notes: The Petersson product of \(f\) with \(G_{2n}G_{k-2n}\) is unfolded to a Dirichlet series involving \(a_m\sigma_{k-1-2n}(m)\). The written range makes one weight negative.
statement: For even \(k\) and integers \(n\) with \(2n\ge4\), \(k-2n\ge4\), pair the holomorphic Eisenstein product with a weight-\(k\) cusp form. Absolute convergence in an auxiliary parameter, followed where necessary by analytic continuation, justifies unfolding. Fourier integration yields a Gamma factor \(\Gamma(k-1)=(k-2)!\), with conjugations consistent with the Petersson convention.
fate: \citet[Rankin method and products of Eisenstein series]{kohnenzagier1984periods} gives this argument. The notebook\textquoteright s inequality \(k/2<n\le k-2\) is incompatible with its chosen weights; an admissible basic range is \(2\le n\le k/2-2\).
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Hecke factorization of the Rankin Dirichlet series
notes: The divisor-sum Dirichlet series factors into two L-values divided by an even zeta-value.
statement: For a normalized level-one eigenform and a complex parameter \(a\), the identity \[\sum_{m\ge1}\frac{a_m\sigma_a(m)}{m^s}=\frac{L(f,s)L(f,s-a)}{\zeta(2s-a-k+1)}\] holds where the series and Euler products converge absolutely and elsewhere by meromorphic continuation. Setting \(s=k-1\), \(a=k-1-2n\) gives the notebook\textquoteright s quotient \(L(f,k-1)L(f,2n)/\zeta(2n)\), interpreted by continuation if needed.
fate: \citet[Rankin product calculation]{kohnenzagier1984periods} uses the Hecke relation to obtain this factorization and derive period comparisons. The identity does not say that \(L(f,2n)/\zeta(2n)\) is independent of \(n\).
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Three rational structures on the cusp-form space
notes: The lecture distinguishes rational Fourier coefficients and rational even and odd periods, and cites Kohnen--Zagier under the title ``Modular forms with rational coefficients.
statement: The Fourier expansion defines a rational structure on level-one cusp forms. Period polynomials, decomposed by parity, give two further rational structures after choosing the appropriate period scalings; Hecke equivariance relates them. The critical-period length for a weight-\(w\) form is \(w-2\), so writing \(S_{2k}\) while keeping the range \(0,\ldots,k-2\) mixes conventions.
fate: The explicitly cited work is \citet{kohnenzagier1984periods}, whose actual title is \emph{Modular forms with rational periods}, published in 1984, not a new 1987 result. It contains the rational-structure comparison rather than the claimed equality of all normalized critical values.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: The rooted orientable gluing numbers
notes: The lecture returns to pairings of \(2n\) polygon sides and counts them by the genus of the glued surface.
statement: The same numbers \(\epsilon_g(n)\) of 1986-700.2 are used: all sides retain their cyclic labels and each pair is glued with opposite induced boundary orientation. Euler\textquoteright s relation is \(V-n+1=2-2g\), hence \(V=n+1-2g\). Pictures suggesting prohibitions on special side pairings must be separated from the unrestricted Harer--Zagier count.
fate: \citet[Theorem~2]{harerzagier1986euler} gives the already established formula. The matrix computation below uses the unrestricted pairing ensemble, including adjacent pairings; imposing the pictured restrictions would define a different enumeration.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Gaussian integration by parts and Wick contractions
notes: A Gaussian Hermitian matrix integral and an integration-by-parts identity produce pairings of the factors in a trace.
statement: For a centred Hermitian Gaussian matrix with covariance \(\mathbb E M_{ij}M_{kl}=N^{-1}\delta_{il}\delta_{jk}\), Wick\textquoteright s rule pairs entries and each contraction contributes that covariance. Equivalently, Gaussian integration by parts differentiates a polynomial observable against its covariance. The measure is normalized to expectation one; treating all complex off-diagonal entries as independent real entries would give wrong constants.
fate: \citet[matrix-integral proof of Theorem~2]{harerzagier1986euler} and \citet[Gaussian diagrammatics]{bessisitzyksonzuber1980graphical} give this exact combinatorial method, established before the talk.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Topological expansion of a Gaussian trace moment
notes: Index cycles are identified with vertices of the glued polygon and the power of \(N\) records genus.
statement: With the covariance just specified, \(\mathbb E[N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}M^{2n}]=\sum_{g=0}^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}\epsilon_g(n)N^{-2g}\). For a pairing, the number of free index loops is \(V=n+1-2g\), while the \(n\) propagators and normalized trace contribute \(N^{-n-1}\). This is a finite identity for every positive integer \(N\), not merely an asymptotic expansion.
fate: This is the exact matrix interpretation in \citet[proof of Theorem~2]{harerzagier1986euler}. It connects to the earlier planar-enumeration occurrence 1982-565.1.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Eigenvalue density and Hermite polynomials
notes: Diagonalization, Vandermonde determinants and orthogonal polynomials reduce the matrix moment to one-dimensional Gaussian integrals.
statement: For a Gaussian Hermitian ensemble, write the Vandermonde as a determinant of monic Hermite polynomials orthogonal for the chosen Gaussian weight. Integrating all but one eigenvalue gives the one-point density as the Gaussian weight times \(\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}P_j(x)^2/h_j\). Its \(2n\)-th moment equals \(\mathbb E\operatorname{Tr}M^{2n}\). The choice \(e^{-x^2}\) versus \(e^{-x^2/2}\) rescales both the polynomials and the moments.
fate: \citet[Gaussian integral computation]{harerzagier1986euler} gives this reduction. The notebook shifts Gaussian conventions and indices; these cannot be combined without rescaling.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Stochastic quantization as an alternative matrix method
notes: A remark attributes a Markov-process approach to Parisi.
statement: The identifiable method realizes a Euclidean field or matrix distribution as an invariant law of a Langevin process, with noise and drift satisfying the appropriate fluctuation-dissipation relation. For a matrix model, existence of the invariant probability and convergence need hypotheses on the potential. This remark does not specify a new stochastic dynamics.
fate: The seminar had already recorded stochastic quantization in 1982-565.2. Its role here is an alternative computational viewpoint, while the actual enumeration proceeds by the Gaussian integral; see the established graphical framework in \citet{bessisitzyksonzuber1980graphical}.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: The Harer--Zagier moment generating function
notes: Two generating formulas are written with double-factorial and normalization shifts that conflict with the zeroth moment.
statement: Let \(C_n(N)=\sum_g\epsilon_g(n)N^{n+1-2g}\), with \(C_0(N)=N\). Then, as a formal power series, \[1+2\sum_{n\ge0}\frac{C_n(N)}{(2n-1)!!}x^{n+1}=\left(\frac{1+x}{1-x}\right)^N,\quad (-1)!!=1.\] Equivalently \(\sum_{N\ge0}C_n(N)t^N=(2n-1)!!\,t(1+t)^n/(1-t)^{n+2}\). These are unnormalized polynomial moments; dividing by powers of \(N\) gives the normalized trace moments.
fate: \citet[Theorem~2 and generating-function proof]{harerzagier1986euler} gives the exact generating identity. The constant and first coefficients are decisive normalization checks; the recorded formula cannot use \((2n)!!\) with the same moments.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Closed genus formula and the Harer--Zagier recursion
notes: The lecture extracts a coefficient of a power of a hyperbolic-tangent expression to obtain the genus count.
statement: For \(0\le2g\le n\), \[\epsilon_g(n)=\frac{(2n)!}{(n+1)!(n-2g)!}[u^{2g}]\left(\frac{u/2}{\tanh(u/2)}\right)^{n+1}.\] Equivalently, \((n+1)\epsilon_g(n)=(4n-2)\epsilon_g(n-1)+(2n-1)(n-1)(2n-3)\epsilon_{g-1}(n-2)\), with the usual zero conventions and \(\epsilon_0(0)=1\). In particular genus zero gives Catalan numbers.
fate: These are \citet[Theorem~2 and displayed recurrence]{harerzagier1986euler}. The theorem was published in 1986, so the March 1987 presentation is expository. The square-root substitution in the notebook needs a factor-of-two correction to agree with the \(u/2\) convention.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Maps with triangular faces and a marked polygonal boundary
notes: Variants add triangular faces, fix a \(2n\)-sided boundary and genus, or introduce two colours and an interface length.
statement: A formal matrix model with a cubic interaction and an insertion \(\operatorname{Tr}M^{2n}\) generates orientable maps with triangular interaction vertices and one marked boundary, sorted by genus. More colours use several matrices and mixed covariances. Exact coefficient extraction depends on rooting and whether the specified polygons are faces of the primal or dual map.
fate: The graphical construction is established in \citet{bessisitzyksonzuber1980graphical}; the Ising specialization is \citet{kazakov1986ising}. These references verify a method for the variants, not one unique numerical formula, because the notebook leaves the counting conventions unstated.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: The Euler product and completed Riemann zeta function
notes: Beilinson lists the Euler product, meromorphic continuation with a single pole at 1, and the symmetric completion \(\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\).
statement: The Euler product converges absolutely for \(\operatorname{Re}s>1\). The zeta function continues meromorphically to \(\mathbb C\), with one simple pole at 1, and \(\Lambda(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\zeta(s)\) satisfies \(\Lambda(s)=\Lambda(1-s)\). The completed function itself has poles at both 0 and 1; only \(\tfrac12s(s-1)\Lambda(s)\) is entire.
fate: These are classical facts reviewed through the local-global integral method in \citet[Sections~2--4]{kudla2003tate}. Tate\textquoteright s thesis circulated in 1950 and was printed in 1967; the source distinguishes those dates.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Archimedean and p-adic local zeta integrals
notes: The Gamma factor is described as a Mellin transform of a Gaussian; the nonarchimedean analogue uses the characteristic function of \(\mathbb Z_p\setminus\{0\}\), called an open subgroup.
statement: With additive normalization \(e^{-\pi x^2}\) and multiplicative measure \(dx/|x|\), the real local integral is \(\int_{\mathbb R^\times}e^{-\pi x^2}|x|^s\,dx/|x|=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\). With \(\operatorname{vol}(\mathbb Z_p^\times)=1\), \(\int_{\mathbb Q_p^\times}1_{\mathbb Z_p}(x)|x|_p^s\,d^\times x=(1-p^{-s})^{-1}\) for \(\operatorname{Re}s>0\). The set \(\mathbb Z_p\setminus\{0\}\) is not a multiplicative subgroup.
fate: \citet[local zeta integrals, Sections~2--3]{kudla2003tate} records these factors and the Haar conventions. Kirillov\textquoteright s volume analogy is heuristic: the volume of an \(s\)-ball has a different Gamma expression, even under analytic continuation in dimension.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Trivial zeros and Bernoulli special values
notes: The functional equation gives simple zeros at negative even integers, and \(\zeta(1-n)=-B_n/n\) is stated at negative arguments.
statement: For \(n\ge1\), \(\zeta(-2n)=0\) and the zero is simple. For integers \(m\ge2\), \(\zeta(1-m)=-B_m/m\), using \(B_1=-1/2\); the omitted \(m=1\) case must be handled separately because \(\zeta(0)=-1/2\). The simplicity at negative even integers uses the functional equation together with nonvanishing of the positive real zeta value.
fate: The analytic continuation in \citet{kudla2003tate} and the Bernoulli calculation reproduced in \citet[Section~2]{gelbart2012reciprocal} support the corrected conventions. These facts predate the lecture.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Regularized power sums and the choice of local parameter
notes: The notes write \(\zeta(-n)=\sum k^n=(t\,d/dt)^n(1-t)^{-1}|_{t=1}\), clarified as the first regular term.
statement: The divergent power sum cannot be evaluated by ordinary substitution. A compatible finite-part prescription uses \(t=e^{-u}\) and the constant term at \(u=0\) of \(\sum_{k\ge1}k^n e^{-ku}\); that constant is \(\zeta(-n)\). Taking instead the constant Laurent coefficient in \(t-1\) is a different operation and generally gives another answer. The regularization parameter must be part of the statement.
fate: The Bernoulli generating-function method underlying the special-value formula is explicit in \citet[Section~2]{gelbart2012reciprocal}. The notebook does not specify a parameter; its abbreviated equality is therefore not literally correct as an ordinary series or a coordinate-free finite part.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Borel regulators and derivatives at negative even integers
notes: The corrected line relates \(\zeta^{\prime}(-2n)\) to the covolume of the image of \(K_{4n+1}(\mathbb Z)\) in \(\mathbb R\).
statement: For \(n\ge1\), the torsion-free part of \(K_{4n+1}(\mathbb Z)\) has rank one. Under the Borel regulator with the corresponding Tate normalization, its image is a lattice in \(\mathbb R\), and the nonzero leading zeta-value \(\zeta^{\prime}(-2n)\) agrees with its regulator covolume up to a nonzero rational factor and the declared orientation convention. Torsion is killed by the real regulator.
fate: \citet[Section~6, especially~6.2--6.4]{borel1977zeta} proves the commensurability statement; the paper was received in November 1976 and published in 1977. The notebook\textquoteright s replacement of \(\zeta(1-2n)\) by a derivative at \(-2n\) is mathematically meaningful and should be preserved.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: p-adic interpolation and the missing measure regularization
notes: The displayed identity makes \((1-p^{n-1})\zeta(1-n)\) a moment of one \(\mathbb Z_p\)-valued measure on \(\mathbb Z_p^\times\), with no auxiliary factor.
statement: The Kubota--Leopoldt construction interpolates Euler-factor-removed zeta or Dirichlet L-values on the appropriate components of p-adic weight space. The zeta branch has a pole and is naturally a pseudomeasure; a bounded measure requires a regularizing factor. For example, in the convention of the cited source and even \(n\ge2\), Mazur\textquoteright s bounded measure satisfies \(\int x^{n-1}d\mu_{1,c}=-(1-c^{-n})(1-p^{n-1})\zeta(1-n)\), where \(c>1\) is prime to \(p\).
fate: The original interpolation is \citet{kubotaleopoldt1964}; the explicit bounded-measure formula and its distinction from the unbounded Bernoulli distribution are read in \citet[equations~(2.1), (2.12)--(2.13)]{gelbart2012reciprocal}. The notebook omits both the regularization and the character-component conventions.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Components of p-adic weight space
notes: The units are split into \((1+p\mathbb Z_p)\) and the \((p-1)\)-st roots of unity, giving \(p-1\) components of the character space.
statement: For odd \(p\), \(\mathbb Z_p^\times=\mu_{p-1}\times(1+p\mathbb Z_p)\). Continuous p-adic characters split according to their finite character on \(\mu_{p-1}\); each component is parametrized analytically by the character on the pro-p factor. For \(p=2\), the corresponding decomposition is \(\{\pm1\}\times(1+4\mathbb Z_2)\), so the written odd-prime formula must not be used unchanged.
fate: \citet[discussion of weight space and the Iwasawa algebra]{gelbart2012reciprocal} makes the character decomposition explicit in the interpolation construction. The prime restriction is missing from the notes.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Riemann hypothesis and prime distribution
notes: The final two numbered topics are RH and its connection with the distribution of primes, without an attempted proof.
statement: The precise named conjecture is \(\operatorname{Re}\rho=1/2\) for every nontrivial zero \(\rho\) of \(\zeta\). Explicit-formula estimates relate the zero locations to the error in prime-counting functions; the prime number theorem by itself is much weaker than RH.
fate: This repeats the conjecture behind record 700. \citet{clay2026riemann} lists RH as unsolved; no resolution is inferred from the adjacent exposition of known analytic continuation.
present_status: Open as of 12 November 2026; the notebook gives a topic heading, not a new equivalent criterion or claimed solution.
worth: Its role is to identify the common unsolved target of the two lectures; an attempted proof is outside a bounded critical annotation.

title: Finite-image Artin representations and ramified Euler factors
notes: A continuous complex representation of the absolute Galois group is localized at primes; inertia and Frobenius are introduced, followed by the unramified determinant factor.
statement: A continuous finite-dimensional representation \(\rho:G_{\mathbb Q}\to GL(V)\) with the usual complex topology has finite image. It is unramified outside finitely many primes. At every prime, the Artin factor is \(L_p(\rho,s)=\det(1-p^{-s}\rho(\mathrm{Fr}_p)|V^{I_p})^{-1}\), with a consistent arithmetic-Frobenius convention. The choice of decomposition group changes the data by conjugacy. The notebook formula on all of \(V\) applies at unramified primes.
fate: \citet[Introduction]{gunhazrasahu2025artin} gives the full inertia-invariant definition and finite-Galois setup. The formulation is classical; the 2025 paper is used to verify the exact general convention and current status, not as the origin of Artin theory.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Dirichlet and Dedekind examples of Artin formalism
notes: One-dimensional characters give Dirichlet functions; inducing the trivial character from \(G_K\) gives \(\zeta_K\); direct sums multiply L-functions.
statement: For a finite-order one-dimensional character of \(G_{\mathbb Q}\), the Artin L-function is the primitive Dirichlet L-function associated with its conductor. For any number field \(K\), \(L(\operatorname{Ind}_{G_K}^{G_{\mathbb Q}}1,s)=\zeta_K(s)\). Moreover \(L(\rho_1\oplus\rho_2,s)=L(\rho_1,s)L(\rho_2,s)\). Using an imprimitive character modulo a larger integer removes extra Euler factors and must be distinguished from the primitive Artin function.
fate: \citet[Section~1]{kudla2003tate} explains primitive and imprimitive characters, while \citet[Section~2]{mantillasoler2019equivalence} gives the induced Galois representation for the Dedekind zeta function.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: An Artin L-function determines the representation but not the field
notes: The notes explicitly distinguish recovering \(\rho\) from \(L(\rho,s)\) and the failure to recover \(K\) from \(\zeta_K(s)\).
statement: Finite-image complex representations of \(G_{\mathbb Q}\) with identical Artin L-functions are isomorphic: equality of Dirichlet coefficients determines unramified Frobenius traces, Chebotarev determines the finite-group character, and complex finite-group representations are semisimple. However nonconjugate subgroups can induce isomorphic permutation representations, yielding nonisomorphic arithmetically equivalent number fields.
fate: \citet[Theorem~2.5, Corollary~2.8 and Section~3 examples]{mantillasoler2019equivalence} gives this argument and explicit field phenomena, tracing the arithmetic-equivalence criterion to Perlis (1977) and Gassmann. The later paper confirms rather than originates the notebook\textquoteright s distinction.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Artin holomorphy
notes: All complex Artin functions are said to be meromorphic; for nontrivial irreducible \(\rho\), holomorphy everywhere is conjectured.
statement: Brauer induction gives meromorphic continuation to \(\mathbb C\) of every finite-image complex Artin L-function. Artin\textquoteright s conjecture asserts that \(L(\rho,s)\) is entire when \(\rho\) is nontrivial and irreducible. Trivial summands must be excluded because they contribute a Dedekind-zeta pole. Monomial representations and many further classes are known, but the general conjecture remains open.
fate: \citet[Introduction and Theorems in Section~1]{gunhazrasahu2025artin}, published 17 February 2025, explicitly distinguishes the classical meromorphic-continuation theorem from the still-open holomorphy assertion and gives new partial criteria.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, meromorphic continuation is established for all complex Artin representations, while the general nontrivial irreducible holomorphy conjecture is unresolved.
worth: The exact finite-image formulation and the boundary between Brauer meromorphy and entire continuation deserve preservation; no general proof is attempted here.

title: The scope of the l-adic continuation question
notes: For l-adic representations, the notes say that even meromorphic continuation is unknown.
statement: This sentence cannot apply uniformly to arbitrary continuous \(\ell\)-adic representations without additional conditions. To formulate the intended arithmetic problem one needs, at a minimum, a representation unramified outside finitely many places, suitable algebraic Frobenius eigenvalues and a complex realization; the geometric or motivic setting supplies the usual conjectural analytic continuation problem. These hypotheses are not stated in the notebook.
fate: The adjoining Artin discussion, verified in \citet{gunhazrasahu2025artin}, concerns finite-image complex representations and cannot settle this broader question. No specific motivic representation or exact conjecture is identified here.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the unqualified sentence is not a well-defined universal theorem or conjecture. Important geometric cases are known, but none is specified sufficiently here for a precise fate assignment.

title: The completed Artin functional equation
notes: The last formula relates \(L^*(\rho,s)\) to \(L^*(\rho^*,1-s)\), with an epsilon factor containing Gauss sums.
statement: For a finite-image complex Artin representation over \(\mathbb Q\), let \(a_\pm\) be the dimensions of the \(\pm1\)-eigenspaces of complex conjugation and \(A(\rho)\) its Artin conductor. With \(\Gamma_{\mathbb R}(s)=\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\), set \(\Lambda(\rho,s)=A(\rho)^{s/2}\Gamma_{\mathbb R}(s)^{a_+}\Gamma_{\mathbb R}(s+1)^{a_-}L(\rho,s)\). Then \(\Lambda(\rho,s)=W(\rho)\Lambda(\rho^*,1-s)\) meromorphically, where \(|W(\rho)|=1\). If the conductor is omitted from the completion, the epsilon factor depends on \(s\).
fate: The Artin analytic framework in \citet{gunhazrasahu2025artin} distinguishes known functional equations from conjectural holomorphy; the local-global normalization is illustrated in \citet[Sections~3--4]{kudla2003tate}. The notebook has not fixed which conductor factor is absorbed in \(L^*\).
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the precise statement above is established; the qualifications distinguish it from the abbreviated notebook formulation.

title: Fractional-dimensional measures and representation parameters
notes: Gelfand mentions a work on integral fractional-linear transformations of the upper half-plane and sets carrying measures of intermediate Hausdorff dimension, in connection with a series of representations.
statement: The notes identify neither the work nor the acting subgroup, invariant or quasi-invariant measure, and representation functor. A relation between dimension and a principal or complementary-series parameter is a plausible theme, but there is no unique theorem or conjecture to reconstruct from the sentence.
fate: Searches for the 1986--1987 combinations of Gelfand, Hausdorff measures, fractional-linear actions and representation series did not recover an exact source. The nearby multifractal literature is only thematic and is deliberately not substituted for the missing reference.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the exact referent remains unidentified. No claim of mathematical nondevelopment follows from this negative identification result.

title: Factors arising from representations of infinite-dimensional groups
notes: The word ``hypothesis introduces the claim that factors arise from representations of infinite-dimensional groups.
statement: To turn this into a mathematical conjecture one must specify the class of groups, representations, generated von Neumann algebras, factor types and any universality assertion. Without those restrictions the statement is either a broad observation or a tautological realization using unitary groups; the notebook gives no discriminating condition.
fate: No precise publication match is asserted. The statement is preserved as a research-program remark adjacent to factor classification, not converted into an invented universal classification problem.

title: Uniqueness of the hyperfinite type III1 factor
notes: The notes say physics produces factors of type \(III_\infty\), of which exactly one is hyperfinite.
statement: The recognizable theorem is uniqueness, up to isomorphism, of the injective (equivalently, in the separable setting, hyperfinite) type \(III_1\) factor with separable predual. There is no standard Connes type \(III_\infty\); the subscript \(\infty\) also occurs in the conventional name \(R_\infty\) for the unique factor, which may explain the notation.
reconstruction: Type \(III_1\), separability and injectivity are the editorial reconstruction of the recognizable uniqueness statement. The manuscript\textquoteright s type label is retained in notes rather than silently corrected.
fate: \citet[Section~2]{haagerup1987bicentralizer} completes the uniqueness proof; the paper was received on 21 January 1985 and printed in April 1987. \citet[publisher description of the 1985--1986 lectures]{wright1989uniqueness} confirms circulation before the March 1987 meeting. This is therefore E, not a new conjecture by Gelfand.

title: Factors, attractors, chaos, and characteristic functions
notes: A list juxtaposes factors, attractors, chaos, Hausdorff measures and characteristic functions.
statement: The list records proposed connections among operator algebras, dynamics and fractal measures. It specifies no map, equality, invariant or question; each named theory has many inequivalent ways of interacting with the others.

title: KdV as a Lax compatibility condition
notes: The displayed equation is \(u_t+6uu_x+u_{xxx}=0\), while the spectral equations use \(L=\partial_x^2+u\) and \(A=4\partial_x^3+6u\partial_x+3u_x\). The free wave is \(e^{ikx+4ik^3t}\).
statement: For this pair, compatibility \(L_t=[A,L]\) gives \(u_t=6uu_x+u_{xxx}\). A free solution with wave number \(k\) has spectral eigenvalue \(-k^2\) and time factor \(e^{-4ik^3t}\). The standard KdV convention in the first line is recovered by reversing time and making the same change throughout the pair. The potential and eigenfunction must be smooth enough for the differentiations.
fate: The inverse-scattering and dressing framework is classical and is reviewed in \citet[Section~2, equations~(25)--(31)]{zakharovshabat1974scheme}. The notebook combines two opposite time conventions. This is a correction of a faithfully recorded formula, not a new integrability claim.

title: Marchenko dressing and its solvability conditions
